ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch published a listicle of Halloween costume ideas aimed at tech professionals, suggesting people dress as AI agents, coding vulnerabilities, or tech industry personalities. ai-at-work.title: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
ai-at-work.excerpt: Big Tech is pouring billions into AI infrastructure, but mounting debt, negative cash flow, and growing investor skepticism are raising questions about the sustainability of the AI spending boom.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Big Tech companies are spending massive amounts on AI infrastructure while racking up debt and negative cash flow, and investors are getting nervous about whether this can actually pay off. Digital workplace leaders need to pay attention because this directly affects whether the enterprise AI tools they're planning to deploy will actually exist in two years or evaporate like every other tech bubble. After three decades watching this cycle, I can tell you that the best time to buy a shovel is when everyone's selling them, not when they're desperately digging.

tools-tech.title: Your Netgear router may be vulnerable to a security exploit – how to check and patch it
tools-tech.excerpt: A vulnerability in some Netgear routers could allow an attacker with access to your network to run malicious commands on the device.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Netgear discovered a security flaw in certain routers that lets someone already on your network execute malicious commands on the device itself. This matters because your corporate network router is basically the front door to everything your organization cares about, and a compromised router turns that door into a revolving entrance for attackers. After three decades watching IT departments struggle with patch management, I can tell you that the routers sitting in server closets are probably the least-updated devices in your entire infrastructure, which means this one's going to hurt more than most.

tools-tech.dwp_take: Smplify launched as a new device management vendor focusing on Apple fleet management, raising $1 million and emphasizing human oversight of AI agents handling device operations. For digital workplace pros, this matters because autonomous AI managing your device fleet without human review is a recipe for cascading disasters that your CEO will somehow blame on IT. Here's the thing though: "human checkpoint" is just a fancy way of saying someone still has to babysit the robot, which means you've added a job, not solved one.

digital-culture.title: What not to do as a CEO pushing AI? Call your workers ‘losers’
digital-culture.excerpt: Plenty of CEOs are bullish on AI and have urged their employees to embrace it enthusiastically. A more unusual approach is to brand your workers as “losers” for not using AI enough. A new investigatio
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Proton CEO reportedly called employees "losers" for not adopting AI fast enough, according to reporting from 404 Media. This matters because it highlights how toxic leadership around emerging tech adoption poisons workplace culture and makes people dig in their heels instead of embracing change. Look, you can't bully people into digital transformation. The CEO just taught his workforce that leadership doesn't understand how to actually get buy-in, which is the whole game here.

digital-culture.title: Lose your job to AI? Here’s what to do if a company wants you back
digital-culture.excerpt: Companies around the world are increasingly citing artificial intelligence when slashing jobs, fueling anxiety that a lot more workers may lose their livelihoods to machines.Microsoft, Barclays Bank a
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies like Microsoft, Barclays, and Kroger are laying off workers and specifically blaming AI for the cuts, adding fuel to legitimate fears about automation eliminating jobs at scale. Digital workplace leaders need to understand this trend because they're often caught in the middle, tasked with implementing the very tools that make roles redundant while managing employee morale and retention. The real irony here is that the same executives using AI to cut costs will probably panic when they realize nobody's left to actually use the systems they bought.

digital-culture.title: How a Contractor’s Claude Agent Got Into the Pentagon
digital-culture.excerpt: This week on Uncanny Valley, we also discuss Anthropic’s IPO filing and the volunteers gearing up to counter ICE at the midterms.
digital-culture.dwp_take: A contractor accidentally deployed an AI agent built with Anthropic's Claude into Pentagon systems, raising serious questions about how classified environments handle third-party AI tools. This matters because many organizations are racing to integrate AI without proper security vetting, and if it can happen at the Pentagon, your company's data governance probably needs a hard look too. The real scandal here isn't that AI got somewhere it shouldn't have, it's that nobody apparently had a process to stop it.
